newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS sugar crop ends 9.1 pct higher - DataNet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS sugar crop ends 9.1 pct higher - DataNet.

text.p: Brazil's center-south sugar harvest reached 10.22 million tonnes in 1996/97, up 9.1 percent from the 9.37 million tonnes produced in 1995/96, said independent consultants DataNet AgriCommodities.
Sugarcane output totalled 227.49 million tonnes, a rise of 11.3 percent on the 204.40 million tonnes harvested in 1995/96 and a new record, it added.
The production figures were to January 1, 1997 and concluded DataNet's estimates of the 1996/97 center-south harvest, the consultants said in a report.
A spokeswoman at the Sao Paulo Sugar and Alcohol Industries Association (AIAA) said AIAA statistics for the fortnightly period to January 1 would possibly be available on Thursday.
As of December 16, sugar output had reached 10.39 million tonnes, according to the last set of AIAA statistics.

According to DataNet, Sao Paulo state showed a 10 percent increase in sugar cane production in 1996/97 while other states in the center-south region - Parana, Minas Gerais, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and Goias - saw a 17 percent rise.
"The expansion of sugar cane should concentrate in these states," DataNet said.

Some 66 percent of the sugar cane in the center-south this year was used in alcohol production, 14 percent was used for sugar exports and the remaining 20 percent was used for the domestic sugar market.

The export market proved to be a great incentive for increased production during 1996/97, not so much because of prices but as a mechanism to capture financial resources at lower interest rates than in the domestic market.
"In this way, sugar exports contributed to the financing of the production of sugar and alcohol for the home market," DataNet said.
"Brazil exported sugar and imported interest rates. This tendency should continue through the next harvest due to the level of interest rates in the domestic market," it added.
DOMESTIC SUGAR MARKET STOCKS DOWN ON LAST YEAR
Center-south sugar stocks are currently around 1.85 million tonnes, 76 percent of which are in Sao Paulo state. This is around 17 percent below stock levels at the same stage last year, DataNet said.

However with an improvement in internal prices, some sugar set aside for exports may be transfered to the domestic market and so DataNet estimates that domestic stocks should only be six percent below last season's levels.
SUGAR EXPORTS SHOULD REACH FOUR MILLION TONNES

The government has so far only authorised the shipment of 3.7 million tonnes free of export tax although it has already said it is going to release a further 500,000 tonnes tax-free which would bring the limit to 4.2 million tonnes.

Given internal prices however, DataNet believes that extra shipments will only be in the order of 250,000 tonnes, bringing total exports to the four million tonne mark, a rise of 14 percent on the 1995/96 crop.
The center-south will next harvest continue to be the largest supplier of low quality white sugar (100 to 150 Icumsa), DataNet added.
ANHYDROUS PRODUCTION UP, HYDROUS OUTPUT DOWN
Anhydrous alcohol production reached 3.8 million cubic meters by the end of December, a rise of 46 percent on output by the same stage in the 1995/96 season.
Hydrous alcohol output was 8.2 million cubic meters, a decrease of 0.5 percent on the 8.24 million cubic meters produced in 1995/96.
WEATHER CONDITIONS THIS HARVEST AND NEXT
Climatic conditions were favorable for the planting and harvest of the 1996/97 crop.
Rainy weather however in the last fortnightly periods led to drop in sugar content aand transport problems.
According to surveys carried out by DataNet, around 3.5 million tonnes of sugar-cane were left unharvested because of the heavy rains in the last six weeks of the campaign.

Currently the weather is very favorable for the development of the new 1997/98 harvest. The center-south harvest normally shows around a four percent growth in production each year given good weather conditions, DataNet said., -- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
